outcome: No public result since 26 January 2024 settles, or moves, the general 3^d bound; the special cases that bear on it were first posted in 2007, 2012, 2022 and 2023, with the Chambers–Portnoy note appearing in its journal only in August 2026, and the in-window preprints I found concern other conjectures or other questions about Hanner polytopes.
problem_asks: (1) For every dimension d, every centrally symmetric d-dimensional polytope has at least 3^d nonempty faces, counting faces of every dimension from 0 to d, the polytope itself included and the empty set excluded. (2) The statement asks for the least possible value of this face count, so it also asks that 3^d be the minimum, that is, attained; the cube and the Hanner polytopes attain it, and this part is not in dispute in any source I read. Not asked by the bullet: (a) the equality characterisation, which some literature statements add (Chor 2025, Conjecture 1.1: equality iff a linear image of a Hanner polytope; Freij et al. 2012: Kalai suggested Hanner polytopes are the only equality cases); (b) Kalai's two stronger conjectures B and C, which he stated alongside A. Polytopes are read as convex, as in the sources.

events.what_happened: Sanyal, Werner and Ziegler posted 'On Kalai's conjectures concerning centrally symmetric polytopes' (arXiv 0708.3661, 27 Aug 2007). Theorem 1.1 proves Kalai's conjectures A (the 3^d bound) and B for every centrally symmetric polytope of dimension d ≤ 4; they show conjecture C fails in dimension 4, and B and C fail for all d ≥ 5. Published in Discrete Comput. Geom. 41 (2009), no. 2, 183–198. The paper does not state a status for A in d ≥ 5.
events.revisions: v1 27 Aug 2007; v2 30 Sep 2007 (current arXiv version). Journal: Discrete Comput. Geom. 41 (2009), no. 2, 183–198 (DOI 10.1007/s00454-008-9104-8, from search listing).
events.delivers: Conjecture A (at least 3^d nonempty faces) for all centrally symmetric convex polytopes of dimension d ≤ 4. Conjectures B and C are refuted (C in dimension 4; B and C for d ≥ 5); those refutations do not touch A.
events.remains: The 3^d bound for every centrally symmetric polytope of dimension d ≥ 5. The equality characterisation (not asked by the bullet).

events.what_happened: Richard P. Stanley, 'On the number of faces of centrally-symmetric simplicial polytopes', Graphs and Combinatorics 3 (1987) 55–66. Proves a conjecture of Björner on the h-vector of centrally symmetric simplicial polytopes, which implies the Bárány–Lovász lower bounds. Sanyal–Werner–Ziegler state that 'the work of Stanley implies A and B for simplicial and thus also for simple polytopes'. I did not read Stanley's paper: the copy on his website is a scanned image that the fetch tool could not read, and the klein.mit.edu address failed a certificate check.

events.remains: Centrally symmetric polytopes that are neither simplicial nor simple.

events.what_happened: Freij, Henze, Schmitt and Ziegler, 'Face numbers of centrally symmetric polytopes from split graphs' (arXiv 1201.5790). Confirms the 3^d conjecture for Hansen polytopes of split graphs, all of which have at least 3^d nonempty faces. The Hanner polytopes in this family, with exactly 3^d faces, correspond to threshold graphs. They also construct a new family of such Hansen polytopes with exactly 3^d+16 nonempty faces.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version, v1, 27 Jan 2012. Journal: Electron. J. Combin. vol. 20, issue 2, article #P32 (listing read; the year 2013 is from search results).
events.delivers: The 3^d bound for every Hansen polytope of a split graph, a subclass of centrally symmetric polytopes; equality exactly for the threshold-graph ones (Hanner polytopes).
events.remains: Every centrally symmetric polytope outside the Hansen-of-split-graphs class.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper (vol. 20(2), #P32); referees not named on the listing read

events.directly_checkable: The split-graph Hansen polytopes are explicit combinatorial objects built from the graph, so the 3^d count for a given graph can be checked by counting faces (the paper's method is combinatorial; I did not check any instance).
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for the subclass. The 3^d+16 family is above the bound, so it is not a counterexample.
events.object: Hansen polytopes H(G) of split graphs G, explicit combinatorial constructions. Those from threshold graphs are Hanner polytopes with exactly 3^d nonempty faces. A further explicit family of Hansen polytopes has exactly 3^d+16 nonempty faces (construction not read in detail).

events.what_happened: Gregory R. Chambers and Elia Portnoy, 'A note on Kalai’s 3^d Conjecture' (arXiv 2211.09215, first posted 16 Nov 2022). Proves the bound (at least 3^d faces, counting all dimensions) for a centrally symmetric d-polytope C that is symmetric about each hyperplane through the origin normal to a vector of some orthogonal basis of R^d (arXiv abstract: 'if there are d hyperplanes with orthogonal normal vectors so that C is symmetric about all of them'). Journal: Electron. J. Combin. 33(3) (2026), #P3.24, DOI 10.37236/13956. The ar5iv render of the arXiv text states the conjecture as 'at least 3^d faces', says it is known for d ≤ 4, for polytopes all of whose faces are simplices, and for Hansen polytopes of split graphs, and says 'this result was independently proved by R. Sanyal and M. Winter'.
events.revisions: v1 16 Nov 2022 (listing only; the v1 PDF is unreadable, so v1 text was not compared); v2 5 Aug 2023 (current arXiv version, '4 pages'). Journal: EJC 33(3) (2026) #P3.24, published online 7 Aug 2026 per Crossref article record (issue record gives 3 Jul 2026). Received and accepted dates are not in the record.
events.delivers: The 3^d bound for every centrally symmetric convex d-polytope that is symmetric about d hyperplanes with pairwise orthogonal normals. Unconditional polytopes (symmetric about all coordinate hyperplanes) are a case of this; Sanyal–Winter describe Chambers–Portnoy as giving another proof of the inequality part for unconditional polytopes (see disputes).
events.remains: Centrally symmetric polytopes without d mutually orthogonal symmetry hyperplanes. Whether it also covers locally anti-blocking polytopes is disputed (see disputes). The equality characterisation (not asked).

checked_by.what_they_did: Cite Chambers–Portnoy and say its proof of the inequality part for unconditional polytopes 'has simultaneously appeared'. This is a comparison, not a check of the argument.

events.doubts: I found no specific error in the argument. The arXiv abstract page as fetched reads 'at least 3^d facets', while the EJC page and the ar5iv render read 'faces' (see disputes). Scope attribution conflicts across three sources (see disputes).
events.direction: Supports the conjecture: proves the inequality for the orthogonal-symmetry class. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Raman Sanyal and Martin Winter, 'Kalai’s 3^d conjecture for unconditional and locally anti-blocking polytopes' (arXiv 2308.02909, first posted 5 Aug 2023). Gives short proofs that s(P) ≥ 3^d, with equality exactly for the Hanner polytopes, for unconditional P (invariant under reflection in every coordinate hyperplane) and, more generally, for locally anti-blocking P ('looks like an unconditional polytope in every orthant'). Revised 14 Oct 2023 and 21 Apr 2024. Journal publication not identified.
events.revisions: v1 5 Aug 2023; v2 14 Oct 2023; v3 21 Apr 2024 (the last is inside the window but is a revision, not a first argument). The HTML v3 carries an internal date line of 24 Aug 2026 that the fetch summary reports, inconsistent with the stamp; not relied on.
events.delivers: The inequality ≥ 3^d for unconditional polytopes and for locally anti-blocking polytopes (presented as the more general class), with equality characterised as the Hanner polytopes in both classes.
events.remains: Centrally symmetric polytopes outside these two classes; the general equality characterisation (not asked); the flag conjecture (a different question).

events.direction: Supports the conjecture: proves it for two classes, with Hanner polytopes as the equality cases. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Dmitry Faifman, Constantin Vernicos and Cormac Walsh, 'Volume growth of Funk geometry and the flags of polytopes' (arXiv 2306.09268, first posted 15 June 2023). Conjectures that the Holmes–Thompson volume of Funk balls in centrally symmetric domains is minimised by Hanner polytopes; proves this for unconditional domains; gives large-radius asymptotics for polytopal Funk geometries whose leading term counts flags. The conjecture is described as interpolating between Mahler's conjecture and Kalai's flag conjecture. The page does not mention the 3^d conjecture. Discarded: a different question (volume and flags).
events.revisions: Single version v1, 15 June 2023. Journal: Geom. Topol. 29 (2025) 3773–3811, DOI 10.2140/gt.2025.29.3773. The journal date (10 Oct 2025) is from a search snippet; the journal PDF was unreadable.
events.delivers: Results on Funk-volume and flag counts for centrally symmetric domains, including the unconditional case. Nothing on the number of nonempty faces, so nothing on the 3^d bound.

events.direction: Different question. Its Hanner-polytope conjecture is for Funk volume, not face counts, so it neither supports nor cuts against the 3^d bound.

events.what_happened: Adam Bohn, Yuri Faenza, Samuel Fiorini, Vissarion Fisikopoulos, Marco Macchia and Kanstantsin Pashkovich, 'Enumeration of 2-level polytopes' (arXiv 1703.01943, 6 Mar 2017). Enumerates all combinatorial types of 2-level polytopes in dimensions up to 7. The abstract and the visible text (through Section 6.2 of a longer, truncated render) do not mention Kalai's conjecture or the 3^d bound. A search-result summary said the paper reports that all 2-level centrally symmetric polytopes up to dimension 7 validate Kalai's 3^d conjecture; I could not confirm this.
events.delivers: Unverified. If the search summary is right, a finite computer check of the bound for the subclass of 2-level centrally symmetric polytopes up to dimension 7. That would be finitely many instances of a universal claim, so it would not move the general conjecture.
events.remains: All of the general conjecture, and every dimension above 7 for any class.
events.doubts: The only support for a 3^d check is an unverified search summary. The text I read does not contain it; the unread part (after Section 6.2) might.
events.direction: If confirmed, consistent with the conjecture on a finite subclass. No counterexample is reported in any source I read.

events.what_happened: Sergey Avvakumov and Alfredo Hubard, 'Cubulating the sphere with many facets' (arXiv 2503.18047, 23 Mar 2025). For each fixed d ≥ 3, constructs cube complexes homeomorphic to the d-sphere with n vertices and Ω(n^{5/4}) facets, disproving a conjecture of Kalai that the number of faces of cubical spheres is maximised by boundaries of neighbourly cubical polytopes. This is a different Kalai conjecture (cubical spheres, maximal face numbers). Discarded.
events.delivers: Disproves a Kalai conjecture about maximal face numbers of cubical spheres. Says nothing about the minimum face count of centrally symmetric polytopes.
events.direction: Different question; it does not cut for or against the 3^d bound.
events.object: Cube complexes homeomorphic to the d-sphere with n vertices and Ω(n^{5/4}) facets (d ≥ 3 fixed, n large), constructed explicitly according to the abstract; the body was not read.

events.what_happened: Arnon Chor, 'Kalai’s flag conjecture for locally anti-blocking polytopes' (arXiv 2507.22284). Proves Kalai's full flag conjecture for locally anti-blocking polytopes: a centrally symmetric d-polytope has at least 2^d·d! full flags, with equality iff it is a linear image of a Hanner polytope. Its introduction restates the 3^d conjecture as Conjecture 1.1 (with the equality clause) and says: 'Recently, Sanyal and Winter, and independently Chambers and Portnoy, proved the 3^d conjecture for locally anti-blocking polytopes.' Discarded as a result on the 3^d bound: it is a flag count, and its 3^d content is a citation.
events.delivers: A flag-count bound for locally anti-blocking polytopes, with the Hanner equality case. Not a face count. Its 3^d statement is a citation of two earlier papers, not a new result.
events.remains: The flag conjecture beyond locally anti-blocking polytopes; the 3^d bound for general centrally symmetric polytopes.
events.doubts: Its attribution of the locally anti-blocking 3^d result to Chambers–Portnoy conflicts with the Sanyal–Winter and Chambers–Portnoy texts (see disputes). I read only the first ~100,000 characters of a ~303,600-character render. No engagement was found in my searches, which are not exhaustive.
events.direction: On flags: consistent with the Hanner-equality pattern. On 3^d: makes no new claim.
events.object: No new object. The equality cases in the flag statement are the (generalised) Hanner polytopes.

events.what_happened: Tomer Milo, 'Asymptotics for face numbers of certain Hanner polytopes, with applications' (arXiv 2603.03861, 4 Mar 2026; v2 23 Apr 2026). Abstract: asymptotics for the number of faces of a certain family of Hanner polytopes; as a corollary it comes close to saturating the FLM inequality for certain parameters. The abstract does not mention Kalai's conjecture. Discarded: a different question on the asymptotics of a family, not a bound on the minimum.
events.delivers: Asymptotic face counts for a family of Hanner polytopes, per the abstract. Not a bound on the minimum face count and not a statement about the 3^d conjecture.
events.doubts: Hanner polytopes have exactly 3^d nonempty faces (Sanyal–Werner–Ziegler; Freij et al.), yet Milo's abstract speaks of asymptotics for 'the number of faces' of a family of Hanner polytopes. That tension is unresolved: it may mean a different count (an f-vector entry or a generalised family). The body was not read.
events.direction: Different question; by its abstract it does not bear on the 3^d bound's direction.

events.what_happened: Jesús A. De Loera, Ethan X. Fang, Shengtao Guo, Junwei Lu and Hailun Zheng, 'On Unavoidable Faces of High-Dimensional Polytopes' (arXiv 2609.00397, 31 Aug 2026). Concerns Kalai's cube–simplex conjecture (for large d, every polytope has a simplex ℓ-face or a cube k-face); proves finiteness of the simple-polytope threshold for ℓ ≥ 2, k ≥ 3, and improves a bound on 3-faces of rational polytopes. Acknowledgements state that the Odin Automatic AI Research Agent was used as a sounding board and to generate code for the computer-assisted portion, and that the final proofs were written and verified by the authors. Not about the 3^d conjecture: no mention of 3^d, centrally symmetric polytopes or Hanner polytopes in the text read. Discarded for this bullet; recorded because it is AI-involved and on a Kalai conjecture.
events.delivers: Results on Kalai's cube–simplex conjecture. Nothing on the 3^d bound.
events.doubts: A search-result summary said the AI agent 'suggested the initial proof' behind results that were later improved. That sentence is not in the text I read; only the sounding-board sentence is quoted here. I read about 100,000 of ~127,000 characters.
events.direction: Different question; no direction on the 3^d bound.

disputes.summary: Which class each paper proved, for the locally anti-blocking and orthogonal-hyperplane results. Chambers–Portnoy (ar5iv render of arXiv 2211.09215): their orthogonal-hyperplane theorem is 'independently proved by R. Sanyal and M. Winter'. Sanyal–Winter (arXiv 2308.02909 v3): 'Another proof of the inequality part for unconditional polytopes due to Chambers and Portnoy has simultaneously appeared'. Chor (arXiv 2507.22284 v2): 'Recently, Sanyal and Winter, and independently Chambers and Portnoy, proved the 3^d conjecture for locally anti-blocking polytopes.' These do not agree. Chambers–Portnoy's hypothesis (orthogonal hyperplanes of symmetry) does not obviously contain locally anti-blocking polytopes, which are defined orthant by orthant; I found no theorem covering both. Unresolved; recorded as found.

Who refuted Kalai's conjectures B and C using Hansen polytopes of split graphs. Wikipedia says Freij et al. (2013) used these polytopes to disprove the stronger conjectures. Freij et al. (arXiv 1201.5790) say 'Two of these, conjectures B and C, were refuted by Sanyal et al. in 2009', and that these Hansen polytopes 'served as counter-examples to conjectures B and C'. The primary text supports the second reading. Minor, but relevant to attribution.

Chambers–Portnoy abstract: the arXiv abstract page as fetched (current v2) reads 'at least 3^d facets', while the EJC page and the ar5iv render read 'faces'. The v1 PDF has a section headed 'Facets are distinct', which suggests an earlier facet-counting version. The theorem counts faces ('adding up all the faces of all dimensions'). Likely a typo in the arXiv abstract text; I did not check it visually.

Simultaneous posting: Chambers–Portnoy's v2 and Sanyal–Winter's v1 are both dated 5 Aug 2023. Neither claims priority over the other; Sanyal–Winter say C–P appeared 'simultaneously', and C–P say S–W 'independently' proved the result.

summary: Kalai's 3^d conjecture, stated as the least number of nonempty faces of a centrally symmetric polytope being 3^d, is still open in general. Wikipedia (fetched; it carries an unsolved-problem box and says the conjecture 'remains open for arbitrary polytopes in higher dimensions') and MathWorld both say it is known for d ≤ 4 and for several classes; I checked these claims at the primary sources where possible. The settled-in-part record is: Sanyal–Werner–Ziegler (2007, DCG 2009) for d ≤ 4 (and refutation of the stronger B and C); Stanley (1987) for simplicial and simple polytopes, as stated by SWZ and Wikipedia (Stanley's text was unreadable to me); Freij–Henze–Schmitt–Ziegler (2012) for Hansen polytopes of split graphs; Chambers–Portnoy (arXiv 16 Nov 2022, journal 7 Aug 2026) for polytopes symmetric about d orthogonal hyperplanes; and Sanyal–Winter (5 Aug 2023) for unconditional and locally anti-blocking polytopes. Each of these is a restricted class, so each leaves the general bound open. The close calls are: (a) whether Chambers–Portnoy also covers locally anti-blocking polytopes, which Chor attributes to them and Sanyal–Winter's own text does not support (see disputes); (b) whether the 2026 journal publication of Chambers–Portnoy counts as a 2026 event; the first-argument rule dates it to 2022, and I have done so; (c) whether the 2017 2-level polytope census counts as a 3^d check up to dimension 7, which I could not verify, since the only support is an unverified search summary and the text I read does not mention the conjecture. In the window (after 26 Jan 2024) I found four preprints on Kalai-related or Hanner-polytope questions: Avvakumov–Hubard (Mar 2025, a different Kalai conjecture on cubical spheres), Chor (Jul 2025, a flag conjecture; it restates the locally anti-blocking 3^d result as a citation only), Milo (Mar 2026, asymptotics for a family of Hanner polytopes; the abstract does not reconcile with the exact 3^d face count of Hanner polytopes, so I left that tension open), and De Loera et al. (Aug 2026, Kalai's cube–simplex conjecture, with the Odin agent named). None bears on the 3^d bound. AI search: no source credits an AI system with any step on this conjecture. The searches covered OpenAI, DeepMind/AlphaEvolve, Gemini, GPT and Claude names, Erdős-problem trackers, Lean formalisation and acknowledgements. The OpenAI primary page returned HTTP 403, and the AI results I saw in 2026 (the Erdős unit-distance disproof reported 20 May 2026; the AlphaEvolve polytope and Gaussian-minima papers; the Odin-assisted cube–simplex paper) concern other problems, so I recorded only the Odin paper, as a discarded event with its AI attribution. Note: the frozen-revision date (26 Jan 2024) matters for the Sanyal–Winter v3 revision (21 Apr 2024), which is not a first argument, and so is not counted in the window.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading the record differently is that the window has produced a real change in the state of the problem: the orthogonal-hyperplane result was published in an EJC issue in July–August 2026, Chor's attribution would put the locally anti-blocking class under the bound by two independent proofs, and MathWorld now lists the 3^d case as partly settled by Chambers and Portnoy (2026). On that reading the bound is settled on the union of the unconditional, locally anti-blocking and orthogonal-hyperplane classes, and the in-window news is that a journal accepted the 2022 note. The reply is that the union still omits general centrally symmetric polytopes, that the journal date is not the first public written argument (§5.1 dates it to Nov 2022), and that the scope claim about locally anti-blocking polytopes is contradicted by the other two texts.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The published Chambers–Portnoy EJC text (readable PDF), to see whether its theorem covers locally anti-blocking polytopes, and to confirm 'faces' vs 'facets' and the date of acceptance. (2) The Sanyal–Winter journal version, if one exists, and its statement of what C–P proved. (3) Stanley's 1987 paper, read directly, to confirm the simplicial count for 3^d. (4) The body of Bohn et al. 2017 after Section 6.2, to confirm or refute the claimed 3^d check up to dimension 7. (5) The body of Milo 2026, to say which face count the asymptotics concern and how it fits the exact 3^d count of Hanner polytopes. (6) A citation sweep of papers citing Sanyal–Winter, Chambers–Portnoy, Freij et al. or Sanyal–Werner–Ziegler after 26 Jan 2024, to find any general-case claim or AI-assisted result that my searches did not reach.
